Concept illustration · Not a product screenshot
01

The problem

Image inference workloads can arrive in bursts. The system needs to match each response to its request while managing the compute capacity behind the queue.

02

The implementation

A Flask service stores uploads in S3, checks DynamoDB for cached predictions, and routes inference through paired SQS queues. EC2 workers load MTCNN and InceptionResnetV1 once per worker.

03

An engineering decision

The controller scales from zero to fifteen workers using queue depth and tracks both pending and running instances. A shared response poller uses request-specific events to match concurrent responses.

04

What it demonstrates

Recorded course tests report 100 correct predictions across 100 concurrent requests, with average response times of 0.32 seconds for cold-cache and 11 milliseconds for warm-cache requests.

05

Context & limitations

Spring 2026 coursework. These are repository-reported course results, not independently repeated benchmarks or production service guarantees. Elastic Vision is the portfolio display name for Elastic Face Recognition on AWS.
